While the dialogue and actions in the story are entirely appropriate for the melancholic and tense atmosphere of two estranged people meeting again, the story lacks any truly surprising turns. The narrative follows a very familiar and predictable trope: one character arrives guarded, keeps their coat on, and claims they can only stay for a "short" time ("until four"), only to gradually soften and reveal they actually have plenty of time ("it's only two-thirty"). Because this progression and the lingering connection between the characters are heavily telegraphed from the moment they order the same drink in unison, the ending feels inevitable rather than subverting expectations in a surprising way.
